page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server includes 2835 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, providing high-speed local disk capacity without requiring external attachments. In benchmark evaluations, the D48ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance profiles. Its memory subsystem achieves a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 3733.43 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 259.05 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches a top-tier throughput of 36.3 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at 275.64 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration and benchmark results indicate high suitability for database operations, web serving, and moderate machine learning tasks. Passmark database operations score at 23458.22, and Redis SET operations reach 84.18 million operations per second. For AI workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable prompt processing speeds of 239.1 tokens per second on a 7B parameter LLM. Given the high density of local storage paired with balanced compute and memory resources, this instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications, relational databases, and enterprise web serving.
